Report_ID: Self-reported improvement in constipation: ≥3 bowel movements per week at 8 weeks
Title: Multi-strain probiotics (Hexbio) containing MCP BCMC strains improved constipation and gut motility in Parkinson’s disease: A randomised controlled trial
Author: Ibrahim et al.
Comment: The paper reports week-8 categories among 22 probiotic and 26 placebo completers: improvement numerators are obtained by summing the explicitly reported ≥3 BM/week categories (probiotic 14 + 3 = 17; placebo 11 + 0 = 11). Per the synthesis contract, event totals use all randomized participants (27 probiotic, 28 placebo), thereby retaining early missing outcomes in the denominator as not improved. The paper did not report a risk ratio for this dichotomized improvement outcome, so RR and its CI are left null. The reported OR 0.22 (95% CI 0.06–0.76) and p=0.017 concern the inverse outcome, BM <3/week, among week-8 assessed participants and are not entered as the requested ITT-denominator improvement effect.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Multi-strain probiotic Hexbio') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: Triple-blind randomized placebo-controlled parallel-group clinical trial
Study Environment: Single-center Parkinson’s and neurology outpatient clinic, Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz, UKM Medical Centre
Medium: Multi-strain probiotic powder sachet versus placebo powder sachet
Participant type: Patients with idiopathic Parkinson’s disease and constipation meeting Rome III criteria
Recruitment source: Parkinson’s and neurology outpatient clinic at Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz
Outcome measurement: Stool diary recording weekly bowel movements; improvement defined for synthesis as the inverse of BM <3 per week, i.e. ≥3 bowel movements per week at 8 weeks
Outcome variable: Self-reported improvement in constipation: ≥3 bowel movements per week at 8 weeks

Title: Probiotics and prebiotic fiber for constipation associated with Parkinson disease: An RCT
Author: Barichella et al.
Comment: Table 3 reports intention-to-treat, multiple-imputation percentages and randomized arm totals, but it does not explicitly report integer responder counts. Therefore group event counts were left null; 43/80 was not inferred or rounded from 53.8%. A conventional count-based risk ratio cannot be calculated verbatim from this report. Topic of Content: Probiotics and prebiotic fiber for constipation associated with Parkinson disease

Title: Probiotics for constipation in Parkinson's disease: A randomized placebo-controlled study
Author: Tan et al.
Comment: This was explicitly described as a post hoc analysis. The Results prose reports rounded percentages (52.9% and 10.5%) and randomized intention-to-treat denominators (34 and 38); the supplied pre-identified effect gives the corresponding event counts as 18/34 and 4/38. The paper did not report a risk ratio, so no RR or RR confidence interval was entered.
